title: Derek Redmond and His Father Finish the Race
text:
Derek Redmond was one of Britain's best 400 meter runners, but injuries had haunted his career. At the 1988 Olympics in Seoul he had to pull out minutes before his first race with an Achilles tendon injury, and he went through many operations afterward.

At the Barcelona Olympics in 1992 he was in form. On 3 August he started the semifinal well. On the back straight, his right hamstring tore, and he fell to the track in agony. The medical staff came with a stretcher. Redmond waved them away. He got up and began hopping toward the finish line, determined to complete the race, while the other runners finished.

In the stands, his father, Jim Redmond, ran down, pushed past the security staff and came onto the track. He put his arm around his son. Derek, weeping, leaned on him, and Jim told him that they had started together and would finish together. With officials hesitating around them, father and son made their way down the home straight while the crowd of some 65,000 rose to its feet. Just before the line, Jim let go so that Derek could cross it alone.

Officially, because he had received help, Redmond was recorded as not finishing. The images of the moment became one of the best known in Olympic history. His career as a runner ended soon afterward.
lesson: When someone we love falls in public, standing beside them matters more than any result. Support at a moment of failure is remembered long after the medals.
source: Barcelona 1992 Olympic results; BBC and contemporary press reports; Derek Redmond's interviews
caveat: Accounts differ slightly on Jim Redmond's exact words.
